- [USER] User requested identification of key points from a specific URL related to the Future Generations Act.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Future Generations Act was passed in Wales in 2015 to improve social, economic, environmental, and cultural well-being through sustainable decision-making.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The purpose of the Future Generations Act is to ensure public bodies in Wales consider the long-term impact of their decisions on future generations' well-being.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Act sets seven well-being goals: a prosperous Wales, a resilient Wales, a healthier Wales, a more equal Wales, a Wales of cohesive communities, a Wales of vibrant culture and Welsh language, and a globally responsible Wales.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Future Generations Act applies to all public bodies in Wales, including government departments, local authorities, health boards, and other public organizations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Public bodies are required to prepare and publish well-being plans that outline how they will contribute to the achievement of the seven well-being goals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Public bodies must carry out assessments of the current and future impact of their decisions on the well-being goals, maximizing positive impacts and minimizing negative impacts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Act requires public bodies to engage with a range of stakeholders, including the public, to inform their well-being plans and assessments.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Welsh Government is required to review and report on the implementation of the Future Generations Act every five years.
